EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A slow moving line of clustering thunderstorms produced high rainfall that caused road and highway flooding in the League City area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was flooding along the Gulf Freeway-Interstate 45 that closed sections of the freeway between the FM 518 and Highway 96 exits.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Flash flooding lead to a road closure.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was a road closure near the intersection of Highway 59 and the 540 Loop in Beasley.
Intermittent flash flooding was reported around the University of Houston - Clear Lake campus.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clusters of rain and thunderstorms formed upon smaller scale boundaries over the greater Houston metropolitan area. These slow-moving cells produced upwards of 8 inches of rain over a few hours from downtown into the Medical Center area. This caused major roadway flooding with some water entering structures in the Spring area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Web cameras showed portions of Highway 288 South going under water. Two lanes on I-10 at the 610 Loop were flooded on the west side of Houston. Reports of high water and impassable roadways around NRG Stadium. An underpass at Washington Avenue and Katy Freeway was impassable due to flood waters with significant flooding reported at Highway 290 and Hollister Street.  There was several inches of water in a church near Melrose Park, and there was water in three homes in Spring.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clustering slow-moving thunderstorms moved eastward across southwestern Montgomery County. Rainfall rates of 2 to 3 inches per hour and slow storm movement caused some roadways to go underwater and become impassable.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Several roads in the Magnolia and Stagecoach areas became impassable due to high water. Several water rescues were made from stalled vehicles.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slow moving showers and thunderstorms produced heavy rainfall from the downtown Galveston area to the Port Bolivar area.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Roads were impassable from the Downtown Galveston area to across parts of the Port Bolivar area.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Little movement of clustering rain and storms along the immediate coastline caused flooding on Galveston Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Significant flooding occurred on Galveston Island from Jamaica Beach up into the city of Galveston as over 10 inches of rain fell in some spots. There were numerous road closures with at least one washed out roadway in the town of Jamaica Beach. There were reports of water within  some structures.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Passing thunderstorms produced high enough rainfall rates to induce flooding on Galveston Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There were flooded roads, with reports of water as high as two feet, around Ball High School. Sections of Harborside Drive-SH 275 from Interstate 45 east to Ferry Road were closed due to high water.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slow moving thunderstorms clustered up over the Texas City and La Marque areas and produced localized flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Flooding was reported on the College of the Mainland campus. A few flooded residences had a half of a foot of water in them along Meadowlark Lane in western Texas City and western La Marque. There were numerous street flooding reports.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Slow moving thunderstorms clustered up over the Texas City and La Marque areas and produced localized flooding.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Some roads along Dickinson Bayou were flooded including Hughes Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clustering storms focused along an inland-moving warm front. These storms produced localized flooding around Galveston County and Galveston Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There were numerous reports of street flooding on the east end of Galveston Island from Scholes Field eastward towards Ferry Road. High water encroached the dorms at Texas A&M-Galveston on Pelican Island with flooding inundating the Strand and points along Harborside Road towards Ferry Road.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms associated with a slow moving cold front produced flash flooding and some wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Numerous roadways and intersection were flooded around Houston. Some of the flooded locations included the intersections of Alabonson Road and West Little York Drive, Eastex Freeway and Little York along with Jensen Drive and Buck Street at the Interstate 10 and Interstate 69 junction.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms associated with a slow moving cold front produced flash flooding and some wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Flooding was reported at the intersections of Highway 59 and Beltway 8 and at Memorial Drive and Shepard Drive.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms associated with a slow moving cold front produced flash flooding and some wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There were sections of Harborside Drive that became impassable due to high flood waters.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Storms associated with a slow moving cold front produced flash flooding and some wind damage.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There was high flood water that caused the intersection of the Gulf Freeway and Highway 96 to become impassable.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: Clustering storms focused along an inland-moving warm front. These storms produced localized flooding around Galveston County and Galveston Island.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: There were reports of water near homes with flooded cars and roadways in Santa Fe, Dickinson and League City. Some of the flooding occurred as Dickinson Bayou went out of banks at SH 3 near Hughes Road.
